subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw stop propagating all root pnpm overrides into third-party managed npm plugin roots, add conflict validation only, or keep requiring Express 4 plugin packages to ship their own override?
rationale: The code change is not a narrow mechanical bug fix because the current override propagation is also a supply-chain and security policy surface for managed plugin installs.

options.title: Scope host overrides in managed roots
options.body: Preserve only maintainer-approved compatible host overrides in plugin npm projects, add an Express 4/path-to-regexp regression test, and document the boundary.

options.title: Add validator-only diagnostics
options.body: Detect the Express 4/path-to-regexp conflict during install or startup and emit an actionable error while leaving package ownership unchanged.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned workaround
options.body: Require affected plugin packages to ship their own override or migrate to Express 5, and close the OpenClaw-side policy change as not planned.

recommendation.title: Scope host overrides in managed roots
recommendation.body: Preserve only maintainer-approved compatible host overrides in plugin npm projects, add an Express 4/path-to-regexp regression test, and document the boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This login is most directly connected to the current managed override propagation and recent plugin install security work.
